propositions: /rerun and recheck-review requests are volatile queue-only events that disappear on process loss before dequeue, leaving Gerrit votes and stale local dedup rows that cause reconciliation to skip the revision.

After process loss, reconciliation checks local voted state before querying Gerrit and skips revisions with surviving stale dedup rows regardless of actual Gerrit state, blocking the owed review from resuming.

The approved repair resets each acceptance path to write neutral LLM-Review: 0 to the exact revision first, verify no nonzero vote remains across all accounts, then reset budget and enqueue the forced event; the reset-emitted comment-added event serves as the durable Gerrit marker.

Reconciliation must query Gerrit before local dedup; a verified no-vote result clears only the exact stale row and invokes the voter, while a Gerrit read error preserves dedup and holds the cursor for retry.
Contributor text cannot select the label value or mint PASS/BLOCK; only the privileged reset operation writes the fixed neutral value 0, and affirmative/refusal replies remain label-free.
The held-out stateful test proves an old nonzero vote plus stale dedup is recovered by one reconcile pass consuming the reset-emitted event after process loss and an empty replacement queue.
